parts.text: Which claim about this arrangement is correct?

options.text: The lamp glows, because both cell terminals are joined to the lamp.
The lamp glows with only Wire 1 from the positive terminal to the lamp.
The lamp does not glow, even though both cell terminals are joined to the lamp.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem:
Kabir connects a small lamp to one cell with copper wires. Wire 1 joins one end of the lamp to the positive terminal. Wire 2 joins the other end of the lamp to the negative terminal.

Answer both parts.

part_answers.answer: A complete path needs both cell terminals joined to the lamp so current can flow through it.

teacher.key_rationale: The lamp glows when both terminals of the cell are connected to the lamp, forming a complete circuit. One wire alone or denying glow when both are joined miss that condition.
